chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: The ghusl of janābah is obligatory, and the ghusl of the menstruating woman when she becomes pure is obligatory, and the ghusl of the woman in istiḥāḍah is obligatory: if she has used cotton padding and the blood passes through the cotton, then ghusl is upon her for every two salats, and for al-fajr there is a ghusl. But if the blood does not pass through the cotton, then ghusl is upon her once every day, and wudu (ablution) for every salat. And the ghusl of the woman in nifās is obligatory, and the ghusl of the deceased is obligatory, and the ghusl of one who touches a deceased person is obligatory.

key_terms.الْكُرْسُفَ: cotton padding used to determine the extent of bleeding
key_terms.الْوُضُوءُ: ritual ablution required for each salat in the stated case
key_terms.غُسْلُ الْجَنَابَةِ: the ritual bath required after janabah

ai.seo_question: In which cases is ghusl obligatory according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states the obligatory cases of ghusl, including janabah, menstruation after purification, istiḥāḍah under specified conditions, nifās, washing the deceased, and touching a deceased person. It is a jurisprudential text on ritual purity that outlines when ghusl is required and when wudu (ablution) suffices alongside it.
